thread:
maya: Heads-up: quick incident — noticed cross-org reads on project configs after yesterday's RBAC role rename. Pinning here.
jon: Got it. How many customers affected?
maya: security-bot flagged 4 tenants with reads from actors in other orgs. I ran a quick audit query, dropped it below.
maya: ```
SELECT * FROM audit_logs
WHERE resource_type='project' AND action='get' AND actor_org != resource_org
AND ts >= '2026-03-19T02:00:00Z'
ORDER BY ts DESC;
```
security-bot: ALERT: anomalous_cross_org_read detected — 4 resources — trace id abc123 — auto-created ticket #INC-2026-0320
aisha: :eyes: can we confirm whether this is a UI bug or backend auth change?
devops: We rolled the RBAC role rename last night to unify project:viewer -> project.read. The migration script had a default grant applied to 'org-admin' role due to a bad join.
jon: Oof. Any immediate mitigation?
devops: I removed the default grant at 02:45 UTC and pushed a hotfix, but some tokens may have cached perms. Recommending token revocation for suspected sessions + forcing reauth.
maya: Can you post the exact SQL that caused the join bug?
devops: ```
UPDATE role_grants rg
SET permission = 'project.read'
FROM org_roles oroles
WHERE oroles.name = 'org-admin'
AND rg.stub = TRUE; -- stub caused default grant to propagate
```
aisha: We should rotate the KMS key used for project config encryption just in case key access paths were abused. Anyone touched key policies?
devops: I modified key alias mapping in KMS to add iam:PassRole for a service account during deploy. That might be the vector. Rolling that back now.
sre-oncall: I can run a scan for cross-org KMS access. Also will tail audit logs for any active decrypt calls referencing other orgs.
jon: Notify affected customers? Legal?
product-ops: Drafting notices now. Want to confirm scope first — are secrets exfiltrated or just config reads?
maya: So far only config metadata reads. No decrypt calls observed in last 6h per quick KMS query. But we need full forensic run.
security-bot: UPDATE: Forensic job enqueued. Correlation id f7e9. Counting reads: 37 cross-org reads across 4 orgs since 02:00 UTC.
aisha: Assigning triage owners: maya for auth rollback verification, devops for KMS policy rollback + key rotation, jon for customer comms + legal loop, sre-oncall for logs + live mitigation.
devops: Estimate for rollback verification: 1h. Key rotation ETA 2h (will require brief config reload).
jon: If we have to rotate keys that will affect Dedicated customers — coordinate window with support.
maya: I pushed a canary rollback to RBAC migration v0.9.1, verifying token cache invalidation now. Found 12 sessions with stale perms, invalidated them.
sre-oncall: I see decrypt attempts from an actor in org-B at 02:17 UTC but they failed with AccessDenied. So no decrypt success — good.
aisha: :lock: good news. Next: produce postmortem template and include timeline.
product-ops: We will wait for full forensic report before sending external notice. Internal noti to CS now.
maya: Forensic artifacts: saved partial audit dump to s3://redwood-forensic/incidents/INC-2026-0320.tar.gz
devops: Rolling back key policy done at 03:15 UTC. Initiating key rotation, will coordinate with ops for short restart.
jon: Scheduling customer call if forensic shows config exposure. Hold on comms until 1st hour update.
security-bot: INC-2026-0320 status: mitigated (controls restored). Next step: postmortem in #postmortems and a follow-up CR to add tests preventing default grants in migrations.
maya: I'll open the CR now: link to PR -> https://git.internal/redwood/rbac-migrations/pulls/112
aisha: Also add a unit test and an integration test hitting audit logs in CI.
devops: Note: we will add a KMS policy guard in deploy pipeline to block iam:PassRole changes without security approval.
jon: Thanks all. Great quick response. Let's sync 30m for a quick rundown before all-hands.
